target_name: Three-year cover of capex and maturing debt
rationale: A genuinely untested permutation within a heavily mined family with clear diagnostic purpose, but the stated "dimensional repair" is overstated since `dlc` is a balance-sheet stock and `TS_SUM(dlc,3)` only proxies three years of rollover under a strong assumption, while `che` remains a point-in-time stock against three-year flows.

target_name: Three-year unadjusted cover of capex and maturing debt
rationale: The motivating claim is economically wrong — `TS_SUM(DELTA(WC,1),3)` telescopes to the three-year *level* change in working capital, which grows systematically with the firm rather than washing out, so the accrual adjustment is if anything more consequential at this horizon — and stripped of that rationale the proposal is a minor ablation of an existing archive ratio.

This is the third numerator swap in an already twice-evaluated SUMRANK pairing (accrual-adjusted leg fmb 3.98/alpha 4.6%, gross-profit leg fmb 2.65/alpha 3.8%), making it a cosmetic variant whose only differentiator is a ~2pp coverage gain rather than a new mechanism.

target_name: Best single source cover plus utilization
rationale: Same SUMRANK template as prior archive entries, but the pairing is properly diagnosed — a high-alpha/weak-slope sufficiency leg combined with an orthogonal slope-strengthening channel — so the test has a defensible ex ante rationale rather than being arbitrary recombination.

A well-motivated ablation that isolates which leg of the three-way MIN destroys alpha and, jointly with the already-evaluated additive version, cleanly separates conjunctive from averaging aggregation — the most informative test in this batch despite operating inside a saturated family.

Combining the trough numerator with the unadjusted cash-earnings simplification is a legitimate first-time pairing of two separately validated changes with a real coverage benefit, though it is a two-ingredient swap in an existing ratio and is mislabelled `novel` when it is plainly a ratio.
